dict.string: An Alfred workflow to fuzzy find files/directories using fzf and fd

# frozen_string_literal: true
require "json" require "time"
file = File.expand_path "#{ENV['alfred_workflow_data']}/fzf-search-history.txt"
# A search is recorded once, when one of its results is chosen, and repeating it # moves the existing record rather than adding another. Older history files # predate that: they were written on every keystroke, so the same search appears # many times over, alongside every prefix typed on the way to it. Collapse # repeats here, keeping the most recent time each search was made, so those files # read as a list of searches too. searches = {} if File.exist?(file) File.foreach(file) do |line| recorded_at, search = line.split("|", 2) next if search.nil? search = search.strip next if search.empty? searches[search] ||= recorded_at.strip end end
def last_searched(recorded_at) "Last searched #{Time.parse(recorded_at).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}" rescue ArgumentError, TypeError recorded_at end
# No "type" here: the argument is a search to run again, not a path. items = searches.map do |search, recorded_at| { "valid": true, "title": search, "subtitle": last_searched(recorded_at), "arg": search } end
if items.empty? items << { "title": "No searches recorded yet", "valid": false } end
jsonout = {"items": items}.to_json
print jsonout

# frozen_string_literal: true
require "json" require "time" require "fileutils" require "shellwords" require "open3" require "digest"
# Package/Bundle extensions (default list) PACKAGE_EXTENSIONS = ['.app', '.bundle', '.framework', '.plugin', '.kext', '.key', '.pages', '.numbers', '.sketch', '.xcodeproj', '.playground', '.photoslibrary', '.xcassets']
# Add custom extensions from environment variable custom_extensions = ENV['package_extensions'].to_s.strip unless custom_extensions.empty? custom_exts = custom_extensions.split(',').map(&:strip).reject(&:empty?) custom_exts.each do |ext| ext = '.' + ext unless ext.start_with?('.') PACKAGE_EXTENSIONS << ext unless PACKAGE_EXTENSIONS.include?(ext) end end
# fd 8.4.0 and later print directories with a trailing path separator # ("/Applications/Mail.app/"), so strip it before matching the extension. def is_package?(path) name = path.sub(%r{/\z}, "") PACKAGE_EXTENSIONS.any? { |ext| name.end_with?(ext) } end
def is_inside_package?(path) PACKAGE_EXTENSIONS.any? { |ext| path.include?("#{ext}/") } end
# macOS stores filenames in either NFC or NFD, and both forms sit side by side in # the same tree: a name saved by one app may spell an accented or voiced # character as a single code point, another as a base character followed by a # combining mark. fzf matches bytes, so a query typed in NFC, which is what an # IME produces, cannot find a name stored in NFD, and vice versa. # Expand each token into an fzf OR group covering both spellings. # # This has to be done per token. fzf's OR binds tighter than the implicit AND # between tokens, so "a | a2 b | b2" means (a OR a2) AND (b OR b2), which is what # we want, while wrapping the whole query would give a AND (a2 OR b) AND b2. # Tokens that are identical in both forms - anything ASCII, including fzf's own # operators - are passed through untouched. def unicode_variants(token) nfc = token.unicode_normalize(:nfc) nfd = token.unicode_normalize(:nfd) nfc == nfd ? token : "#{nfc} | #{nfd}" rescue ArgumentError, Encoding::CompatibilityError # Invalid byte sequence: fall back to matching the token as typed. token end
# fd and fzf are run directly rather than through a shell, so nothing the user # types can be interpreted as a command. The option strings in the workflow # configuration are still shell-flavoured, so they are split the way a shell # would - and a leading ~ is expanded here, since no shell is left to do it. def split_options(str) Shellwords.split(str.to_s).map do |token| token.start_with?("~") ? File.expand_path(token) : token end rescue ArgumentError => e STDERR.puts "fzf workflow: ignoring malformed options #{str.inspect} (#{e.message})" [] end
# fd's stderr is surfaced to the Alfred debugger instead of being discarded, so # permission errors and bad options are diagnosable. def run_fd(fd_args) out, err, _status = Open3.capture3(*fd_args, binmode: true) STDERR.puts(err) unless err.empty? out end
# Walking the search path is by far the most expensive part of a search, and the # script filter re-runs on every keystroke, so the same tree is walked again for # every character typed. When cache_ttl is set, the candidate list is reused for # that many seconds. def candidate_list(fd_args, ttl) return run_fd(fd_args) if ttl <= 0
dir = ENV["alfred_workflow_cache"].to_s return run_fd(fd_args) if dir.empty?
FileUtils.mkdir_p(dir) unless File.directory?(dir) # Everything that changes what fd would print is part of the key, so changing a # search path or an exclude pattern cannot serve a stale list. file = File.join(dir, "candidates-#{Digest::MD5.hexdigest(fd_args.join("\x00"))}.txt")
return File.binread(file) if File.exist?(file) && (Time.now - File.mtime(file)) < ttl
list = run_fd(fd_args) # Write to a private temporary file and rename it into place. Alfred terminates # the running script on every keystroke, so a plain write could be interrupted # partway through and leave a truncated list to be served as if it were whole. tmp = "#{file}.#{Process.pid}" File.binwrite(tmp, list) File.rename(tmp, file) # A run killed before the rename leaves its temporary file behind; clear out any # that are old enough to be certain no live run still owns them. Dir.glob("#{file}.*").each do |orphan| begin File.unlink(orphan) if Time.now - File.mtime(orphan) > 300 rescue SystemCallError nil end end list rescue SystemCallError => e STDERR.puts "fzf workflow: cache unavailable (#{e.message})" run_fd(fd_args) end
def filter_candidates(fzf_path, query, list) out, _err, _status = Open3.capture3(fzf_path, "-e", "--filter", query, "--read0", "--print0", stdin_data: list, binmode: true) # fzf exits non-zero when nothing matches, which is not an error here. out.split("\x00").map { |path| path.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8) } end
# Locate an executable, tolerating Alfred's minimal PATH. # Priority: user-specified env var -> common Homebrew paths -> login shell lookup -> nil. def find_command(name, env_key) user_path = ENV[env_key] if user_path && !user_path.empty? expanded = File.expand_path(user_path) return expanded if File.executable?(expanded) end
candidates = [ "/opt/homebrew/bin/#{name}", # Apple Silicon Homebrew "/usr/local/bin/#{name}", # Intel Homebrew "/usr/bin/#{name}", # System ] found = candidates.find { |p| File.executable?(p) } return found if found
detected = `/bin/bash -lc 'command -v #{Shellwords.shellescape(name)}' 2>/dev/null`.strip return detected if !detected.empty? && File.executable?(detected)
nil end
fd_path = find_command("fd", "fd_path") fzf_path = find_command("fzf", "fzf_path")
missing_tools = [] missing_tools << "fd" unless fd_path missing_tools << "fzf" unless fzf_path unless missing_tools.empty? tools = missing_tools.join(" and ") brew = missing_tools.join(" ") message = "#{tools} not found. Install via Homebrew (brew install #{brew}), or use Alfred Preferences > Workflows > Alfred Gallery > Resolve Dependencies." STDERR.puts message print({ "items" => [{ "title" => "#{tools} not installed", "subtitle" => "Install via Homebrew: brew install #{brew} — or use Alfred's Resolve Dependencies", "valid" => false }] }.to_json) exit 0 end memorize = ENV["memorize"].to_i == 1 ? true : false treat_packages_as_dirs = ENV["treat_packages_as_dirs"].to_i == 1 ? true : false
search_paths = ENV["search_home"] || ENV["search_path"] search_paths = search_paths.split(/\s*;\s*/) search_paths = search_paths.map do |search_path| path = File.expand_path(search_path) File.exist?(path) ? path : nil end.compact.uniq
fd_options = ENV["fd_options"] || "" fd_options_conf = ENV["fd_options_conf"] || "" exclude_patterns = ENV["exclude_patterns"] || "" exclude_options = exclude_patterns.split(/\s*;\s*/).reject(&:empty?).flat_map { |p| ["--exclude", p] } num_candidates = ENV["num_candidates"] || "100" num_candidates = num_candidates.to_i num_candidates = 100 if num_candidates <= 0 cache_ttl = ENV["cache_ttl"].to_i
keys = ARGV.join(" ").gsub(" ", " ").split(/\s+/) query = +"" keys.each do |key| if /\A(?:\^|\-)(?:d|dir|directory)\z/ =~ key fd_options = " -p -t d" elsif /\A(?:\^|\-)(?:f|file)\z/ =~ key fd_options = " -p -t f" else query << key + " " end end
query.strip!
# With no keys at all there is nothing to match on, and an empty fzf filter would # return the entire search path. Say so instead. Past searches live under the # fzf-history keyword rather than here. Note that a bare directive such as "^d" # is a real search and does not land here. if keys.empty? print({"items" => [{"title" => "Input search keys (space separated)", "valid" => false}]}.to_json) exit 0 end
# What fzf is asked to match. The plain query is kept for the history file. fzf_query = query.split(/\s+/).map { |token| unicode_variants(token) }.join(" ")
# Store original fd_options to determine search type. Note that the default # search passes both -t f and -t d, so "includes -t d" alone does not mean the # user asked for directories only. search_type = fd_options.strip directory_only = search_type.include?('-t d') && !search_type.include?('-t f') file_only = search_type.include?('-t f') && !search_type.include?('-t d')
# Build exclude patterns for packages when treat_packages_as_dirs is off unless treat_packages_as_dirs # Exclude package contents. The '**/' prefix is required: an fd --exclude glob # that contains a slash is anchored to the search root, so '*.app/*' on its own # would only match packages sitting directly in it. package_excludes = PACKAGE_EXTENSIONS.flat_map { |ext| ["--exclude", "**/*#{ext}/*"] } # Additionally exclude packages themselves when searching for directories only if directory_only package_excludes += PACKAGE_EXTENSIONS.flat_map { |ext| ["--exclude", "**/*#{ext}"] } end else package_excludes = [] end
# A file-only search still has to offer packages, which are directories. Ask fd # for both types in one pass and tell them apart afterwards by the trailing # separator, rather than walking the whole tree a second time just to find them. collect_packages = file_only && !treat_packages_as_dirs fd_type_options = split_options(fd_options) fd_type_options += ["-t", "d"] if collect_packages
# One fd invocation covers every search path, so candidates from different paths # are ranked against each other and the limit applies to the search as a whole # rather than to each path separately. fd_args = [fd_path, ".", *search_paths, *fd_type_options, *package_excludes, *exclude_options, *split_options(fd_options_conf), "-0"]
results = filter_candidates(fzf_path, fzf_query, candidate_list(fd_args, cache_ttl))
# Post-process results when treat_packages_as_dirs is off unless treat_packages_as_dirs if directory_only # Directory search: exclude packages results.reject! { |r| is_package?(r) } elsif collect_packages # File search: keep files, and keep directories only when they are packages results.select! { |r| !r.end_with?("/") || is_package?(r) } end # For default search (both files and dirs), packages are already included but their contents are excluded end
results = results.first(num_candidates)
items = [] type = "file:skipcheck"
if results.size > 0 results.each do |result| path_split = result.split(File::SEPARATOR) title = File::SEPARATOR + path_split[-2 .. -1].join(File::SEPARATOR) subtitle = path_split[0 ... -2].join(File::SEPARATOR) item = { "valid": true, "type": type, "title": title, "subtitle": subtitle, "arg": result, "icon": { "type": "fileicon", "path": result }, # Lets Alfred preview the result in place with its Quick Look key. "quicklookurl": result } if memorize # uid = Digest::MD5.hexdigest(result) item["uid"] = result end items << item end else items << { "title": "No results found", "valid": false } end
# The search that produced these results, carried alongside them so that the # action which records the history knows what was searched for. The script filter # cannot record it itself: it re-runs on every keystroke, and recording there # means recording every prefix of every query, whether or not anything came of it. jsonout = {"variables": {"fzf_search_key": query}, "items": items}.to_json
print jsonout

# frozen_string_literal: true
require "fileutils"
# Runs when a result is chosen, not while the query is being typed. The script # filter re-runs on every keystroke, so recording there stored every prefix of # every search whether or not anything came of it. Recording here keeps the # searches that actually led somewhere. path = ARGV[0].to_s search = ENV["fzf_search_key"].to_s.strip max_search_history = ENV["max_search_history"].to_i
unless search.empty? file = File.expand_path "#{ENV['alfred_workflow_data']}/fzf-search-history.txt" begin dirname = File.dirname(file) FileUtils.mkdir_p(dirname) unless File.directory?(dirname)
entries = File.exist?(file) ? File.readlines(file) : [] # Repeating a search moves it back to the top rather than adding another # copy: this is a list of searches, not of the times each one was run. entries.reject! do |line| _, recorded = line.split("|", 2) recorded && recorded.strip == search end entries.unshift("#{Time.new} | #{search}\n") entries = max_search_history > 0 ? entries.first(max_search_history) : []
File.open(file, "w") { |f| f.puts(entries) } rescue SystemCallError => e STDERR.puts "fzf workflow: could not record history (#{e.message})" end end
# Pass the path through unchanged so the next action still receives it. print path

An Alfred workflow to fuzzy find files/directories using fzf and fd.
Check out the [README](https://github.com/yohasebe/fzf-alfred-workflow) on the GitHub repository of this workflow.

Number of candidate files/directories shown in Alfred [Default: 100]

Directory (or directories) for recursive search. Multiple paths may be specified, separated by semicolons. [Default: ~]
NOTE: If a home directory is specified, ~/Library will be ignored for better performance; to search within a cloud storage folder such as Dropbox or OneDrive, specify ~/Library/CloudStorage/. (e.g. ~; ~/Library/CloudStorage/)
Check to have Alfred manage order
If checked, Alfred will manage the order of items according to usage. [default = unchecked]
Maximum number of past search history retained. [default = 1000]

If checked, packages/bundles (.app, .graffle, .key, .pages, etc.) will be treated as directories and their contents will be searchable. If unchecked, they will be treated as files and their contents will be excluded from search. [default = unchecked]

Folder/file name patterns to exclude from search results. Separate multiple entries with semicolons. These are passed as --exclude options to fd and apply wherever they appear in the search tree. [default: node_modules;.git;]

Reuse the list of files found by fd for this many seconds instead of walking the search path again on every keystroke. On a large search path this is the difference between a search that takes a second or more and one that is instant, at the cost of files created in the last few seconds not showing up yet. Set to 0 to walk the search path every time. [default: 0, suggested: 60]
